component.name: Gale
component.summary: Mod manager for Thunderstore games, with profiles you can import and share

description.p: This is a community package of Gale, maintained independently. It repackages the official upstream Linux build unmodified. Upstream also publishes a Flatpak of their own, from their own repository at kesomannen.com; this package is an alternative way to get the same build, not a replacement for it, and it uses the same application ID.

Gale is a mod manager for the games hosted on Thunderstore. It keeps each set of mods in a profile, so you can switch between a modded and a clean install, keep separate profiles per playthrough, and hand one to a friend as a code or an .r2z file.

ul.li: Browse and install mods from Thunderstore, with dependencies resolved for you
Profiles you can import, export, duplicate and sync, including profiles exported from r2modman
Per-profile mod configuration edited in the app, and one-click updates for outdated mods
Launch a modded game straight from Gale, including Proton titles
Install from a Thunderstore page through its "Install with Mod Manager" button

description.p: The package is sandboxed. It is granted the Steam directories it has to write mods into, and the ability to start Steam on the host; everything else - profiles, the mod cache, the database and settings - lives under ~/.var/app/com.kesomannen.gale.
Some setups need one more grant; add the ones that apply with "flatpak override":

ul.li: A Steam library on another drive or in a non-default location: flatpak override --user --filesystem=/mnt/games/SteamLibrary com.kesomannen.gale (name the library folder itself)

Importing your existing r2modman or Thunderstore Mod Manager profiles, which live in your host config directory: flatpak override --user --filesystem=~/.config/r2modmanPlus-local:ro com.kesomannen.gale
A non-Steam game directory you point Gale at: flatpak override --user --filesystem=/path/to/the/game com.kesomannen.gale

description.p: One thing behaves differently inside the sandbox: the in-app updater cannot replace the packaged build, so new upstream releases arrive as Flatpak updates instead. Gale detects that it is running in a Flatpak and hides the update button by itself.
